original_question: Let (n_k)_{k>=0} be the increasing sequence of positive integers whose base-2 digit sum S_2(n_k) is even. What is the exact metrical order of the discrepancy of the one-dimensional sequence ({n_k alpha})_{k>=0}?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem 14, posed immediately after Open Problem 13 as the one-dimensional preliminary problem needed for the metrical discrepancy study of a specific Niederreiter-Kronecker hybrid sequence.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper. It correctly identifies the exact subsequence n_k of positive integers with even binary digit sum, it correctly forms the one-dimensional sequence ({n_k alpha}), and it correctly asks for the exact metrical order of its discrepancy. This is essentially Open Problem 14 in Section 3, up to notation and a few implicit details.
missing_details: The paper’s notation is s_2(n) for the sum of digits of n in base 2; the defining condition is s_2(n_k) ≡ 0 mod 2.

Because the problem is metrical, alpha should be quantified explicitly: the intended meaning is for Lebesgue-almost all real alpha (equivalently, almost all alpha in [0,1), since only fractional parts matter).
To make the question stand-alone, the discrepancy should be identified as the discrepancy D_N of the first N terms of the sequence, with N tending to infinity.
The sequence should be stated as a sequence in [0,1), i.e. x_k = {n_k alpha}, where {·} denotes fractional part modulo 1.
If fully self-contained, the discrepancy should be defined explicitly, e.g. D_N((x_k)) = sup over 0 ≤ a < b ≤ 1 of |#{0 ≤ k < N : x_k in [a,b)} - N(b-a)|.

The paper introduces this problem as a necessary first step toward Open Problem 13; that contextual narrowing explains why the one-dimensional formulation should not be broadened beyond this exact subsequence problem.
refined_question: Let (n_k)_{k≥0} be the increasing sequence of positive integers such that s_2(n_k) ≡ 0 mod 2, where s_2(n) denotes the sum of the base-2 digits of n. For Lebesgue-almost every alpha in [0,1), determine the exact asymptotic order, as N → ∞, of the discrepancy D_N of the one-dimensional sequence x_k = {n_k alpha}, namely D_N((x_k)_{k≥0}) = sup_{0≤a<b≤1} |#{0≤k<N : x_k in [a,b)} - N(b-a)|.
justification: The draft matches Open Problem 14 almost verbatim. In Section 3 the paper states Open Problem 14 for the sequence formed from the increasing positive integers n_k whose binary digit sum has even parity. The sentence immediately before Open Problem 14 says that investigating Open Problem 13 first leads necessarily to this one-dimensional problem, so this is the exact target rather than a broader neighboring question. Section 1 supplies the discrepancy setting for sequences in [0,1)^s, so making D_N and fractional parts explicit is the correct way to turn the paper’s terse problem statement into a stand-alone research question. The only substantive implicit ingredient in the draft is the metrical quantifier on alpha, which is inherited from the surrounding Section 3 discussion and stated explicitly in Open Problem 13.
